extracted.intended_audience: heads of executive departments and agencies, agency rulewriters, and OMB staff (Director of the Office of Management and Budget)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for federal agencies to limit regulatory costs and identify offsets when proposing or issuing regulations, including reporting to OMB and inclusion in the Unified Regulatory Agenda. Applies across executive-branch rulemaking and the Presidential budget process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify two repealed regulations per new regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an executive department or agency publicly proposes for notice and comment or otherwise promulgates a new regulation, it shall identify at least two existing regulations to be repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies unless prohibited by law; intended to ensure that for every one new regulation issued, at least two prior regulations be identified for elimination (Sec. 2(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: FY2017 total incremental cost cap (zero net cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fiscal year 2017, the total incremental cost of all new regulations, including repealed regulations, to be finalized this year shall be no greater than zero, unless otherwise required by law or consistent with advice provided in writing by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directed to the heads of all agencies; allows exceptions where required by law or with written OMB Director advice (Sec. 2(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: New incremental costs must be offset by eliminating costs of at least two prior regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new incremental costs associated with new regulations shall, to the extent permitted by law, be offset by the elimination of existing costs associated with at least two prior regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any agency eliminating existing costs under this subsection shall do so in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act and other applicable law (Sec. 2(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of prior regulations must follow APA and law
rubrics_metrics.description: When eliminating existing regulations to offset new regulatory costs, agencies must do so in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act and other applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedural legal constraints on repeal actions used as offsets (Sec. 2(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Director to provide implementation guidance and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall provide heads of agencies with guidance on implementation, including standardizing measurement/estimation of regulatory costs and standards for determining what qualifies as new and offsetting regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance shall address processes for standardizing measurement and estimation of regulatory costs; standards for determining qualifying new and offsetting regulations; standards for determining costs of existing regulations considered for elimination; accounting for costs in different fiscal years; oversight methods for offsets across times or agencies; and circumstances (e.g., emergencies) that might justify waivers. The Director may consider phasing in and updating requirements (Sec. 2(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual submission: identify offsets and approximate costs/savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the Regulatory Plans for fiscal year 2018 and each fiscal year thereafter, the head of each agency shall identify, for each regulation that increases incremental cost, the offsetting regulations described in section 2(c) and provide the agency’s best approximation of the total costs or savings associated with each new regulation or repealed regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires agencies to report offsets and cost/savings approximations in Regulatory Plans (Sec. 3(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Director-approved regulations in the Unified Regulatory Agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Each regulation approved by the Director during the Presidential budget process shall be included in the Unified Regulatory Agenda required under Executive Order 12866 (or successor order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and tracking of Director-approved regulatory actions in the Agenda (Sec. 3(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations must be listed on most recent Agenda or have Director approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise required by law, no regulation shall be issued by an agency if it was not included on the most recent version or update of the published Unified Regulatory Agenda, unless the issuance of such regulation was approved in advance in writing by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents agencies from issuing off-agenda regulations except when statutorily required or specifically approved in writing by the Director (Sec. 3(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director sets agency-specific total incremental cost allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: During the Presidential budget process, the Director shall identify to agencies a total amount of incremental costs that will be allowed for each agency in issuing new regulations and repealing regulations for the next fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No regulations exceeding an agency’s total incremental cost allowance will be permitted in that fiscal year, unless required by law or approved in writing by the Director. The allowance may allow an increase or require a reduction in total regulatory cost (Sec. 3(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'regulation' and specified exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this order the term 'regulation' or 'rule' means an agency statement of general or particular applicability and future effect designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or to describe procedure or practice requirements of an agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions: (a) regulations issued with respect to military, national security, or foreign affairs functions; (b) regulations related to agency organization, management, or personnel; (c) any other category exempted by the Director (Sec. 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation must be consistent with law and appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that the EO does not override statutory requirements or funding constraints (Sec. 5(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order does not create enforceable private rights; does not impair statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States or its entities; and nothing shall be construed to impair the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency or the functions of the Director relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States legal limits on the EO’s effects and preserves agency statutory authority and Director functions (Sec. 5(a) and (c)).
